R2-01.why: Three escalating beats (smash, panic-hide, hunt) give instant chaos plus real tension, and FREEZE/re-hiding/snitching create genuine decisions and funny failure; but the Parent has nothing to do for 2:45 of a 5-min round, and hiding via one auto-pick button with preset hotspots risks feeling like menu selection.
R2-01.fix: Give the Parent a live PARTY-phase role (e.g., upstairs 'working from home' with limited peeks or phone-call interruptions that force kids to freeze) and let kids choose which item to carry (cycle with a tap) so hiding is a choice, not an auto-pick.

R2-02.why: Fart-Together-style shared steering is proven instant comedy and wipeouts are funny not frustrating; a single HOLD button plus one contextual verb is thin per-player agency, and with silent strangers or bot-filled seats the coordination puzzle can collapse into either chaos-only or the bots doing the work.
R2-02.fix: Add readable non-verbal coordination (seat-to-seat 'PULL/STOP' pings, a shared upcoming-hazard strip) and give each seat a distinct skill verb per vehicle so players own a role rather than just holding a button.

R2-03.why: Red-light/green-light tension plus hide-in-plain-sight is a fun loop with zero progression: every second is a move-or-freeze decision, off-plinth risk vs prank reward, noisy pranks as bait, and a Guard role with real skill and limited battery; getting caught mid-pose is funny.
R2-03.fix: Tagged statues must not spectate: make them 'cracked statues' that can trigger one distraction (cuckoo, alarm) or rejoin via a teammate rescue, and cap guard idle by shrinking the map as battery drains.

R2-04.why: Drawing a rune and seeing it fire is strong first-30-seconds juice, misfires are funny, and relic drafting adds run variety; but auto-targeting and no movement mean the optimal play can degrade into spam-tracing, and 1-second fusion timing with voiceless strangers is mostly accidental.
R2-04.fix: Make enemy types demand specific spells/fusions (armored = ice+lightning) and add a 'fusion invite' glow: when one player starts a rune, others see a 1-s window and the suggested partner rune, so fusing becomes an intentional, communicable decision.

R2-05.why: The inspect-with-one-tool shop loop is a decent Papers-Please-lite, but the deduction layer depends on discussion that pings/stamps cannot carry for under-13s, mid-round leavers wreck the 4-8 player social structure, and first 30 s is slow and rule-heavy.
R2-05.fix: Shift deduction from talk to evidence: forgers must physically perform visible actions (back-room trips, tool-misuse tells) that leave auto-logged traces, and make the meeting a quick 15-s icon vote; let forgers have their own satisfying sabotage minigame so the role is fun even when caught.

R2-06.why: The Watcher gets the actually-fun anomaly-spotting job, while the majority (Patrollers) follow an arrow and tap — low agency and low skill; the whole round hinges on one player, so a Watcher who leaves or is inattentive ruins it.
R2-06.fix: Give everyone spotting: Patrollers see subtle anomalies the cameras cannot (sound, smell, touch), and rotate the Watcher seat each night; add Patroller risk/decision (approach vs avoid escalating anomalies) so their half of the info asymmetry is also a game.

R2-07.why: Content Warning's laughs come from voice chat and real screaming; on Roblox with no voice for minors the replay is avatars ragdolling, and the minute-to-minute loop for non-camera holders (walk around, get grabbed) is barely specified.
R2-07.fix: Design the expedition as a game, not a recording: ghost-specific counterplay (each ghost has a rule to bait for a shot), a 'stunt' verb for every crew member that scores in-frame, and emote-driven reactions auto-triggered on scares so replays are funny without voice.

R2-08.why: Per-parcel handling rules (sagging cake, sloshing tank, two-person clock) give immediate readable comedy and failure is funny; but scripted/discrete 'physics' risks feeling fake, and carry-through-obstacles loops get repetitive past a few shifts.
R2-08.fix: Make the wobble feel physical with client-side visual sim tied to server value meter, and add mid-delivery choices (shortcut through the sprinkler yard vs safe long route, hand-off throws between players) to add decisions beyond 'walk carefully'.

R2-09.why: With zero progression the match is: place 3 critters on a 3x3, watch an auto-fight, tap once — roughly a dozen meaningful inputs per 4 minutes; the appeal is almost entirely the breeding/collection meta, which is exactly the progression-masking-a-thin-core pattern.
R2-09.fix: Rebuild the match around per-round economy decisions (Merge-Tactics-style shop, rerolls, merges, item draft) so matches are fun with starter critters, and make the live tap ability a positioning/targeting choice rather than a timing tap.

R2-10.why: Asymmetric bomb/manual information is a genuinely interesting co-op puzzle and the confetti-blast failure is funny; but reducing communication to tapping matching stamps risks turning it into transcription, removing the panicked miscommunication that makes the genre fun, and bot-backfilled partners kill the point.
R2-10.fix: Keep stamps but make the manual require interpretation (conditional branches that depend on what the Hands report), limit stamps per device so players must compress information, and replace bot backfill with a solo 'both screens' practice mode.

R2-11.why: Overcooked-style cascading emergencies with big icons read well without voice, triage creates real decisions, and crashes are spectacular rather than punishing; risk is that each station is a single hold-button task, and the pilot seat is dull.
R2-11.fix: Give stations short distinct actions (aim the extinguisher, carry the patch to the right hole, crank rhythm) and give the pilot choices that create work for crew (dodge storm = fewer hazards but longer route; risky shortcut = fires).

R2-12.why: Spreading fire, collapsing floors and last-second two-person rescues give good tension and triage decisions, but auto-aimed hold-to-spray removes most hose skill and the moment-to-moment can feel like holding a button; the sanctuary collection is doing heavy lifting for long-term motivation.
R2-12.fix: Replace auto-aim with generous manual aim plus water-tank/pressure management and fire types (grease, electrical) needing different tools, so extinguishing is a skill; make critters behave (flee, hide, panic) so rescues are mini-puzzles.

overall_notes: Strongest pure-fun cores are R2-03 (moment-to-moment tension with real decisions for both sides), R2-01, R2-02, R2-04 and R2-11. Recurring problems: idle/one-sided roles (Parent in R2-01, Patrollers in R2-06, caught statues in R2-03), heavy auto-targeting/auto-picking that removes skill (R2-04, R2-12, R2-01), and concepts whose fun assumes voice chat (R2-05, R2-07, R2-10). Veto on R2-09: its match is near-zero-agency and the breeding meta is masking a thin core. R2-06 and R2-07 are not vetoed but are weak on fun as specified.
